title: Gluten-Free Coconut Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft gluten-free coconut cupcakes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake, made moist with coconut milk and topped with coconut-flecked buttercream.
description: These cupcakes use coconut milk instead of regular milk, so every bite stays soft and moist. I tested this batter three times in my own kitchen before the crumb held together without turning gummy. The gluten-free flour blend I use has xanthan gum built in, which helps mimic the structure regular flour gives. If your blend does not have it, add a quarter teaspoon to the dry mix. The frosting is where the coconut flavor really shows up. Toasted coconut flakes fold right into the buttercream, so you get little crunchy bits in every swirl. This batch makes 12 cupcakes, perfect for a potluck where someone always asks for a gluten-free option.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
3/4 cup full-fat canned coconut milk, well shaken
1/2 cup toasted coconut flakes (for frosting and topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl.
Beat softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla and coconut extract.
Alternate adding the flour mix and coconut milk, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until smooth.
Fold in the shredded coconut with a spatula.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For the frosting, beat butter for 2 minutes until pale. Add powdered sugar in two batches, then mix in coconut milk until smooth.
Fold toasted coconut flakes into the finished frosting, then pipe onto fully cooled cupcakes and top with extra flakes.
tips: Toast the coconut flakes in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, so they do not burn.
Shake the canned coconut milk well before measuring, since the fat separates and settles at the top.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting or the buttercream will slide off.
If your gluten-free flour blend has no xanthan gum, add 1/4 teaspoon to the dry ingredients.

faq.question: Can I use coconut cream instead of coconut milk in the batter?
faq.answer: Coconut cream is too thick and will make the batter dense. Stick with canned full-fat coconut milk for the right texture.

faq.question: Why did my gluten-free cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the batter was overmixed or the oven door opened too early. Mix just until smooth and wait until minute 15 to check.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap the butter for a plant-based baking stick in both the cupcake and frosting for a dairy-free version.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving for the best texture.

conclusion: These coconut cream cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still be soft and rich. Bring them to your next gathering and watch the plate empty fast.
